I farm about 10 mu of flat land here in Quzhou, same as my family has for years. My husband and I talked it over — we'll do what we always do: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same plots. That's what everyone in our village grows. The market price is stable enough, and we know how to do it. Wheat goes in the ground in October after the summer maize comes off, maize goes back in June after wheat harvest. Two crops a year on the same land.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the township supply cooperative — the semi-dwarf variety they sell there, not the old seed we used to save. Yield is better. For maize, I always buy hybrid seed. Everyone does now. No point using old varieties.

Fertilizer: I put down what my neighbor Wang puts down, maybe a little more on the wheat because last year the ears looked thin. I apply the base fertilizer before planting and top-dress at jointing for wheat. For maize I side-dress at the big bell stage.

Water: I pump from the well. Wheat needs water four times — before winter, at jointing, heading, and grain filling if it's dry. Maize I water twice — once to get it started, once in the dry August stretch.

I spray once for weeds on the maize and do two rounds on wheat — one herbicide in winter, one fungicide in May when the stripe rust or scab shows up. I watch what the village TV program says about disease alerts.

I rotary-till the wheat field before sowing. For maize I plant straight into the wheat stubble — saves time and diesel money.
